lesson.text: Quick memory: on an orienteering map, what shape marks the start? (A purple triangle.) Today: following a course with a map and a compass.
Set the map: turn it until north on the map points north in the world. With a compass, turn the map until its north lines point the same way as the red end of the needle.
The red end of a compass needle points north. The directions go round clockwise: north, east, south and west, with north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west between them.
A bearing is a direction in degrees, measured clockwise from north: north is 0°, east 90°, south 180° and west 270°. So north-east, halfway between north and east, is 45°.
A map's scale gives real distances. On a 1:5,000 map, 1 cm stands for 50 m. On a 1:10,000 map, 1 cm stands for 100 m. So there, 3 cm on the map is 300 m on the ground.
Pace counting: count each time your left foot lands. That is one pace, two steps. If you take 70 paces to walk 100 m, then 35 paces is about 50 m.

Plan a route: follow a handrail, like a path, a wall or a stream, towards the control. Aim for an attack point, a big feature near it, then go carefully from there. Keep your thumb on the map where you are.
Try it in the world: hide 5 flags, draw their map with a scale and a north arrow, and give a friend the bearings. For real: try a permanent orienteering course in a park.

exercises.prompt: Which way does the red end of a compass needle point?
exercises.hint: It lines up with the Earth's magnetism.
exercises.explain: North: that is how a compass shows you the directions.

exercises.prompt: Setting the map means turning it so north on the map points north in the world.
exercises.hint: Why turn a map before you use it?
exercises.explain: True: then left on the map is left for real, and everything lines up.

exercises.prompt: What is the bearing of east?
exercises.hint: Bearings go clockwise from north, which is 0°.
exercises.explain: 90°: a quarter turn clockwise from north.

exercises.prompt: Match each direction to its bearing.
exercises.hint: Go round clockwise from north, a quarter turn (90°) each time.

exercises.prompt: Which direction is hidden by the question mark?
exercises.hint: Go round clockwise from N: N, NE, E, SE, S, and on.

exercises.prompt: On a 1:5,000 map, 1 cm stands for 50 m. A leg of the course is 6 cm long on the map. How far is it, in metres?
A handrail in orienteering is a line you can follow, like a path or a stream.
exercises.hint: What does a handrail on a staircase help you do?
exercises.explain: True: follow it towards the control, and you cannot get lost.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order to find a control.
exercises.hint: The map must point the right way before you plan.
items: plan a route along a handrail
exercises.explain: Set the map, plan a route, go to the attack point, then find the control carefully.

exercises.prompt: You are lost in a wood. What should you do?
exercises.hint: What is the signal for help, and why stay still?
choices: stay where you are and blow 6 whistle blasts
exercises.explain: Stop and stay put, and blow 6 blasts on a whistle, again each minute: searchers find you faster.

exercises.prompt: You are at the start triangle. Which control is north-east of the start?
exercises.hint: North is up on this map. North-east is up and to the right.
exercises.explain: 3: it is up and to the right of the start.

exercises.prompt: You are walking on a bearing of 90°. You turn right by 90°. What is your new bearing, in degrees?
exercises.hint: Turning right adds to the bearing.

exercises.prompt: Bram takes 70 paces to walk 100 m. How many paces will he count for 250 m?
exercises.hint: 250 m is 2 and a half lots of 100 m.

exercises.prompt: On a 1:10,000 map, how far on the ground is 4.5 cm?
Why choose an attack point before a control that is hard to find?
exercises.hint: Is it easier to find something big, or something small?
choices: it is big and easy to find, and close
it is always the shortest way
exercises.explain: An attack point is big and easy to find, and close to the control, so you only go carefully for the last bit.

exercises.hint: Go three quarter turns clockwise from north.

exercises.prompt: The straight line to the control crosses a steep hill, but a path goes round it. Which is often faster?
exercises.hint: Is climbing a steep hill quick?
choices: the path round, even though it is longer
exercises.explain: The path round: running on a path is often faster than climbing, even if it is longer.
